papers.title: Benchmarking the Impact of Data Leakage on the Performance of Knowledge Graph Embedding Models for Biomedical Link Prediction
papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Knowledge Graphs (KGs) organize complex biomedical knowledge into structured representations of entities and relations. Knowledge Graph Embedding (KGE) models learn compact representations of KGs, and are widely applied for biomedical link prediction. Despite extensive work on KGE models, current evaluations often overlook the issue of data leakage, which can artificially inflate performance and undermine benchmark validity. Data leakage can arise when (1) there is redundancy between training and test sets, (2) the model leverages illegitimate features, or (3) the test set does not accurately reflect real-world inference. Results We assess the impact of data leakage on KGE-based link prediction across three biomedical knowledge graphs, using decoder-only and GNN-based models. We first demonstrate the impact of train-test redundancies and implement a systematic procedure to detect and remove them. Using permutation experiments, we also investigate whether node degree acts as an illegitimate predictive feature, and find no evidence that predictions are driven by degree alone. Finally, we evaluate how well common test set sampling strategies reflect real-world inference in drug repurposing. We compare random and cold-start data splits with an independent test set from Orphanet, and observe a substantial performance drop on the latter, indicating that current benchmarking practices may overestimate how well KGE models generalize to practical applications. Overall, our findings highlight the importance of rigorous benchmark design and careful evaluation of the generalization ability of KGE models for biomedical link prediction. Availability and Implementation Code and results are openly available on GitHub at https://github.com/galadrielbriere/data_leakage_kge_benchmark.git and archived on Zenodo at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21885112

papers.llm_rss_summary_zh:
**摘要与动机**  
知识图谱将复杂的生物医学知识组织成实体与关系之间的结构化表示形式。知识图谱嵌入模型能够学习到这些知识图谱的紧凑表示，因此被广泛用于生物医学领域中的关联预测任务。尽管目前针对这类模型的研究已经十分深入，但现有的评估方法往往忽视了“数据泄漏”这一问题——这种现象可能会人为地提升模型性能，从而削弱基准测试的有效性。数据泄漏通常发生在以下三种情况下：（1）训练集与测试集之间存在冗余信息；（2）模型使用了不合适的特征进行预测；（3）测试集无法真实反映现实世界的推理过程。  

**研究方法与结果**  
我们选取了三个生物医学知识图谱，分别使用仅包含解码器的模型以及基于图神经网络的模型，来评估数据泄漏对关联预测性能的影响。首先，我们验证了训练集与测试集之间的冗余性对模型性能的负面影响，并制定了一套系统化的方法来检测和消除这些冗余信息。通过排列实验，我们还探讨了节点度数是否可能成为不合适的预测特征，但并未发现任何证据表明仅凭节点度数就能准确预测结果。最后，我们分析了常见的测试集采样策略在药物再利用场景中的适用性，将随机抽样方法与基于Orphanet独立数据集的采样方法进行了对比，发现后者会导致模型性能显著下降，这说明现有的基准测试方法可能高估了知识图谱嵌入模型在实际应用中的泛化能力。  

**代码与数据公开**  
我们的研究代码及实验结果已公开发布在GitHub上：https://github.com/galadrielbriere/data_leakage_kge_benchmark.git，同时也在Zenodo平台上进行了存档：https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21885112。

all_papers.title: Benchmarking the Impact of Data Leakage on the Performance of Knowledge Graph Embedding Models for Biomedical Link Prediction
all_papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Knowledge Graphs (KGs) organize complex biomedical knowledge into structured representations of entities and relations. Knowledge Graph Embedding (KGE) models learn compact representations of KGs, and are widely applied for biomedical link prediction. Despite extensive work on KGE models, current evaluations often overlook the issue of data leakage, which can artificially inflate performance and undermine benchmark validity. Data leakage can arise when (1) there is redundancy between training and test sets, (2) the model leverages illegitimate features, or (3) the test set does not accurately reflect real-world inference. Results We assess the impact of data leakage on KGE-based link prediction across three biomedical knowledge graphs, using decoder-only and GNN-based models. We first demonstrate the impact of train-test redundancies and implement a systematic procedure to detect and remove them. Using permutation experiments, we also investigate whether node degree acts as an illegitimate predictive feature, and find no evidence that predictions are driven by degree alone. Finally, we evaluate how well common test set sampling strategies reflect real-world inference in drug repurposing. We compare random and cold-start data splits with an independent test set from Orphanet, and observe a substantial performance drop on the latter, indicating that current benchmarking practices may overestimate how well KGE models generalize to practical applications. Overall, our findings highlight the importance of rigorous benchmark design and careful evaluation of the generalization ability of KGE models for biomedical link prediction. 当出现以下情况时，就可能会发生数据泄露：(1) 训练集与测试集之间存在冗余信息；(2) 模型使用了不合法的特征进行训练；或者 (3) 测试集无法准确反映现实世界中的推理情况。
all_papers.llm_rss_summary_zh:
**摘要与动机**  
知识图谱将复杂的生物医学知识组织成实体与关系之间的结构化表示形式。知识图谱嵌入模型能够学习到这些知识图谱的紧凑表示，因此被广泛用于生物医学领域中的关联预测任务。尽管目前针对这类模型的研究已经十分深入，但现有的评估方法往往忽视了“数据泄漏”这一问题——这种现象可能会人为地提升模型性能，从而削弱基准测试的有效性。数据泄漏通常发生在以下三种情况下：（1）训练集与测试集之间存在冗余信息；（2）模型使用了不合适的特征进行预测；（3）测试集无法真实反映现实世界的推理过程。  

**研究方法与结果**  
我们选取了三个生物医学知识图谱，分别使用仅包含解码器的模型以及基于图神经网络的模型，来评估数据泄漏对关联预测性能的影响。首先，我们验证了训练集与测试集之间的冗余性对模型性能的负面影响，并制定了一套系统化的方法来检测和消除这些冗余信息。通过排列实验，我们还探讨了节点度数是否可能成为不合适的预测特征，但并未发现任何证据表明仅凭节点度数就能准确预测结果。最后，我们分析了常见的测试集采样策略在药物再利用场景中的适用性，将随机抽样方法与基于Orphanet独立数据集的采样方法进行了对比，发现后者会导致模型性能显著下降，这说明现有的基准测试方法可能高估了知识图谱嵌入模型在实际应用中的泛化能力。  

**代码与数据公开**  
我们的研究代码及实验结果已公开发布在GitHub上：https://github.com/galadrielbriere/data_leakage_kge_benchmark.git，同时也在Zenodo平台上进行了存档：https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21885112。

all_papers.primary_summary_raw: Knowledge Graphs (KGs) organize complex biomedical knowledge into structured representations of entities and relations. Knowledge Graph Embedding (KGE) models learn compact representations of KGs, and are widely applied for biomedical link prediction. Despite extensive work on KGE models, current evaluations often overlook the issue of data leakage, which can artificially inflate performance and undermine benchmark validity. Data leakage can arise when (1) there is redundancy between training and test sets, (2) the model leverages illegitimate features, or (3) the test set does not accurately reflect real-world inference. Results We assess the impact of data leakage on KGE-based link prediction across three biomedical knowledge graphs, using decoder-only and GNN-based models. We first demonstrate the impact of train-test redundancies and implement a systematic procedure to detect and remove them. Using permutation experiments, we also investigate whether node degree acts as an illegitimate predictive feature, and find no evidence that predictions are driven by degree alone. Finally, we evaluate how well common test set sampling strategies reflect real-world inference in drug repurposing. We compare random and cold-start data splits with an independent test set from Orphanet, and observe a substantial performance drop on the latter, indicating that current benchmarking practices may overestimate how well KGE models generalize to practical applications. Overall, our findings highlight the importance of rigorous benchmark design and careful evaluation of the generalization ability of KGE models for biomedical link prediction.
